name: Pico Genesis / PicoSure Pro

lead: PicoSure Pro is a 755 nm picosecond alexandrite laser that clinics use for acne scars, pigmented spots, wrinkles and tattoo work, aiming for clearer tone and softer scars. "Pico Genesis" appears on forums and clinic menus as a name for picosecond-style skin treatments.

Picosecond pulses deliver energy in trillionths of a second, which proponents describe as a mainly photomechanical effect that shatters pigment rather than relying on heat. A diffractive lens array can add small zones of skin change for scars and texture. A 2025 prospective single-center study combined it with radiofrequency microneedling for atrophic acne scars, and a 23-person post-market trial was registered.

paras: It is performed in a clinic, usually as a series of sessions spaced weeks apart. Many people choose it for the short recovery. Pigment and tone changes build over a few sessions, and it is sometimes paired with other scar treatments such as RF microneedling.

Short-lived redness and swelling are generally described. Pigment changes are a recognised concern with laser treatments of skin, especially in darker skin types. Long-term comparative data are scarce, and the results reported vary by device and condition.

chain: Skin remodels with fewer side effects
angle.text: Picosecond pulses break up pigment and stimulate skin remodeling with short downtime, leaving clearer tone and softer scars. PicoSure Pro is used for acne scars, pigmented spots and skin texture, and published studies are small.

lead: PicoSure Pro is a picosecond laser system from Cynosure that emits light at 755 nm (an alexandrite laser) and can be fitted with a diffractive lens array. In aesthetic clinics it is used to improve how skin looks: atrophic acne scars, wrinkles and fine lines, and pigmented spots, with the aim of smoother, more even skin and fewer visible marks [1][2].

'Pico Genesis' is a name used in clinic and forum discussion of picosecond skin treatments; this article treats it together with PicoSure Pro, the device for which published research and trial registrations could be found.

With the diffractive lens array, a picosecond pulse is split into many tiny spots that create microscopic injuries in the epidermis, and researchers propose that the skin's repair of these injuries drives the improvement in pigmentation and scars [3]. A 2025 randomized split-face trial in Dermatologic Surgery evaluated the PicoSure Pro with the array plus radiofrequency microneedling for facial atrophic acne scars [1], and a completed 23-participant post-market usability trial was registered for wrinkles, acne scars and benign pigmented lesions [2].

paras: The device is described in the research literature for facial atrophic acne scarring when used with a diffractive lens array, and a registered usability trial listed wrinkles, acne scars, and benign epidermal and dermal pigmented lesions as conditions of interest [1][2].

A 2016 clinical study in Lasers in Surgery and Medicine used a 755 nm picosecond alexandrite laser with a fractional lens array at three energy settings, examining skin by confocal microscopy and biopsy. It found intra-epidermal cavities whose number, density and size depended on the melanin index and energy, and the treated zones exfoliated over about three weeks. The authors attribute the cavities to laser-induced optical breakdown and suggest this injury may stimulate epidermal repair linked with improvements in dyspigmentation and acne scars [3].

A 2025 prospective, single-center, evaluator-blinded, split-face randomized trial published in Dermatologic Surgery enrolled 20 subjects with moderate to severe atrophic facial acne scarring. One face half received the picosecond laser followed by radiofrequency microneedling and the other half microneedling only, over four treatments at four-week intervals. Both halves improved significantly on blinded investigator scar grading and on physician and subject global aesthetic improvement scales, with no significant difference between them at interim time points; the authors state larger trials are required [1].

A post-market usability evaluation of the PicoSure Pro (NCT05102617), started in October 2021 with 23 participants, is registered as completed; it lists wrinkles, acne scars and benign pigmented lesions as conditions [2].

Picosecond laser treatments are discussed in appearance communities as a skin-quality procedure (scars, pigment, texture) and are categorised under hardmaxxing procedures. Little community material was available for this entry.

timeline.event: Lasers in Surgery and Medicine study describes histology after picosecond alexandrite laser with a fractional lens array [3].
Post-market usability trial of the PicoSure Pro starts (NCT05102617) [2].
Randomized split-face trial of picosecond laser plus radiofrequency microneedling for acne scars published [1].
